title: Iliad
author: Homer
description: The foundational epic of Greek literature, depicting the wrath of Achilles during the final year of the Trojan War. Primary source for Greek gods' involvement in mortal affairs.

characters.role: protagonist
Troy's chief defender, killed by Achilles
Achilles' companion, killed by Hector
commander of the Greek forces
watches the war from Troy's walls
second-mightiest Greek warrior
strategist among the Greek leaders
arbiter of the war's course from Olympus
patron of the Greeks, especially Achilles and Odysseus
patron of Troy and Hector

keyScenes.title: The Wrath of Achilles
keyScenes.summary: Agamemnon's seizure of Briseis drives Achilles to withdraw from battle, dooming the Greeks to Trojan advances.

keyScenes.title: Hector and Ajax's Duel
keyScenes.summary: Hector and Ajax fight to an inconclusive draw and part with an exchange of gifts.

keyScenes.title: The Death of Patroclus
keyScenes.summary: Wearing Achilles' armor, Patroclus routs the Trojans before Hector kills him.

keyScenes.title: The Death of Hector
keyScenes.summary: Achilles kills Hector in single combat outside the walls of Troy and drags his body behind his chariot.

keyScenes.title: Priam Ransoms Hector's Body
keyScenes.summary: King Priam comes to Achilles' tent by night to beg for his son's body, and Achilles relents.

readingOrder: Start with Robert Fagles's 1990 translation for a vivid, propulsive verse rendering, or Emily Wilson's 2023 translation for the newest scholarly-accessible option.

title: Odyssey
author: Homer
description: The epic tale of Odysseus's ten-year journey home from Troy, featuring encounters with gods, monsters, and mortals. Essential source for Greek mythology and religious practices.

characters.role: protagonist
his wife, besieged by suitors on Ithaca
visited at Sparta by Telemachus, now reconciled with Menelaus
shade in the underworld who warns Odysseus about Clytemnestra
shade in the underworld
shade who refuses to speak to Odysseus over the arms of Achilles
Odysseus's protector and guide throughout his journey
pursues Odysseus in anger over the blinding of his son Polyphemus

keyScenes.title: The Cyclops' Cave
keyScenes.summary: Odysseus blinds the Cyclops Polyphemus and escapes by hiding his men under sheep.

keyScenes.title: The Descent to the Underworld
keyScenes.summary: Odysseus consults the dead, including the prophet Tiresias and the shades of Achilles and Agamemnon.

keyScenes.title: Circe and the Sirens
keyScenes.summary: Circe turns his men to pigs before aiding him, and he later has himself bound to the mast to hear the Sirens safely.

keyScenes.title: The Stringing of the Bow
keyScenes.summary: Penelope sets a contest with Odysseus's own bow that none of the suitors can even bend.

keyScenes.title: The Slaughter of the Suitors
keyScenes.summary: Odysseus reveals himself and kills the suitors who have besieged his household.

readingOrder: Emily Wilson's 2018 translation is the standout starting point for first-time readers, prized for its clarity and pace; Robert Fagles's 1996 verse translation is the classic alternative.

title: Theogony
author: Hesiod
description: A systematic account of the origin and genealogy of the Greek gods, from primordial Chaos to the reign of Zeus. The definitive source for divine genealogy.

characters.role: youngest child of Cronus who leads the Olympians to victory and becomes king of the gods
eventually becomes Zeus's queen
born from the sea foam after Cronus castrates Uranus

keyScenes.title: The Castration of Uranus
keyScenes.summary: Cronus castrates his father Uranus at Gaia's urging, ending Uranus's tyranny over his children.

keyScenes.title: The Birth of Aphrodite
keyScenes.summary: Aphrodite rises from the sea foam formed where Uranus's severed body fell into the water.

keyScenes.title: Zeus Swallows Metis
keyScenes.summary: Zeus swallows his pregnant consort Metis to forestall a prophecy that her child would surpass him, later giving birth to Athena himself.

keyScenes.title: The Titanomachy
keyScenes.summary: Zeus and the Olympians defeat the Titans in a ten-year war and imprison them in Tartarus.

readingOrder: M.L. West's Oxford World's Classics prose translation of Hesiod is the standard accessible starting point, with a full scholarly introduction to the succession myth.

title: Works and Days
author: Hesiod
description: A didactic poem containing the myth of Prometheus, Pandora, and the Five Ages of Man. Provides insight into Greek religious and moral philosophy.

characters.role: Supreme Olympian ruler who hides fire and prosperity from humankind following Prometheus's deception
Titan champion of mortals who steals fire in a hollow fennel stalk, inciting Zeus's retribution
Messenger god who guides Pandora to Epimetheus and instills within her a shameless mind and deceitful nature
Goddess of wisdom who clothes Pandora in silver robes and teaches her the art of weaving
Goddess of love who sheds irresistible grace and heartbreaking desire upon Pandora's head

keyScenes.title: The Fashioning of Pandora
keyScenes.summary: At Zeus's order, Hephaestus kneads water and clay into a beautiful maiden, Athena robes her, Aphrodite bestows charm, and Hermes names her Pandora because all Olympians gave her a gift: a beautiful plague for men.

keyScenes.title: The Opening of the Storage Jar
keyScenes.summary: Pandora removes the great lid of her jar, dispersing plagues, miseries, and weary labor among mortals, slamming the rim shut while only Hope (Elpis) remains within.

keyScenes.title: The Myth of the Five Ages of Man
keyScenes.summary: Hesiod narrates the moral decline of humanity across five epochs: the peaceful Golden Age, foolish Silver Age, violent Bronze Age, noble Heroic Age at Troy and Thebes, and the bitter Iron Age.

readingOrder: Read lines 42-105 (the myth of Prometheus, Pandora, and the jar) followed directly by lines 109-201 (the Five Ages of Man) to understand Hesiod's view of the human condition.

title: Homeric Hymns
author: Various (attributed to Homer)
description: A collection of thirty-three anonymous hymns celebrating individual Greek deities. Major source for myths of Demeter, Apollo, Hermes, and Aphrodite.

characters.role: Goddess of agriculture whose grief for her abducted daughter withers the crops of the earth
Queen of the Underworld whose eating of the pomegranate seed compels her cyclical return to Hades
Archer god of music and light who slays Python on Mount Parnassus to establish the Delphic Oracle
Trickster infant born at dawn who invents the lyre, steals Apollo's cattle at noon, and plays for Zeus at dusk
Goddess of love compelled by Zeus to desire the mortal Trojan shepherd Anchises, conceiving Aeneas
God of wine and divine ecstasy who turns Tyrrhenian pirate kidnappers into leaping dolphins

keyScenes.title: The Abduction of Persephone and the Eleusinian Rites
keyScenes.summary: Hades seizes Persephone into the underworld; Demeter wanders in mourning, withholds harvest from humanity, and upon Persephone's return teaches holy mysteries at Eleusis.

keyScenes.title: Hermes Crafts the Lyre and Steals Apollo's Cattle
keyScenes.summary: Hours after his birth in Mount Cyllene's cave, baby Hermes scoops a tortoise from its shell, strings it with sheep-gut, sings, and drives Apollo's sacred heifers backwards to baffle pursuers.

keyScenes.title: Dionysus and the Tyrrhenian Pirates
keyScenes.summary: Pirates bind young Dionysus; bands fall away, fragrant wine floods the dark ship, ivy wraps the mast, and the god roars as a lion, causing the crew to jump into the sea as dolphins.

readingOrder: Start with Hymn 2 (to Demeter) for the magnificent narrative behind the Eleusinian Mysteries, followed by Hymn 4 (to Hermes) for divine trickster humor, and Hymn 7 (to Dionysus).

title: Poetic Edda
author: Anonymous
description: A collection of Old Norse poems from the medieval Icelandic manuscript Codex Regius. Primary source for Norse mythology including the Voluspa prophecy and Havamal.

characters.role: dragon-slayer, central to the heroic lays of the second half of the collection
characters.where: Fafnismal, Sigrdrifumal, and the Sigurd lays

characters.role: appears throughout as wanderer, war-god, and seeker of wisdom
trickster present in several mythological poems
protector of gods and men against giants

keyScenes.title: Sigurd Slays Fafnir
keyScenes.summary: Sigurd kills the dragon Fafnir from a pit dug in its path and gains the power to understand birds from tasting its blood.

keyScenes.title: The Waking of Sigrdrifa
keyScenes.summary: Sigurd wakes a valkyrie sleeping behind a wall of flame, who teaches him runes and counsel before their story turns to tragedy.

keyScenes.title: Loki's Flyting
keyScenes.summary: Loki crashes a feast of the gods and insults each of them in turn before being bound as punishment.

keyScenes.title: Thor's Wedding Disguise
keyScenes.summary: Thor dresses as a bride to recover his stolen hammer from the giant Thrym.

readingOrder: Carolyne Larrington's Oxford World's Classics translation (1996, revised 2014) is the standard modern starting point, with notes that untangle the poems' compressed references.

title: Prose Edda
author: Snorri Sturluson
description: A manual of poetics that preserves Norse mythology through three sections: Gylfaginning (mythology), Skaldskaparmal (poetic diction), and Hattatal (verse forms).

characters.role: his slaying of Fafnir is retold as the origin of a kenning for gold
narrates or is described throughout the mythological framing
central figure of several retold myths
engineers Baldur's death

keyScenes.title: The Creation of the World
keyScenes.summary: Snorri recounts how the world was formed from the body of the primordial giant Ymir.

keyScenes.title: Thor's Fishing Trip
keyScenes.summary: Thor goes fishing with the giant Hymir and nearly hauls up the World Serpent, Jormungandr.

keyScenes.title: The Death of Baldur
keyScenes.summary: Loki tricks the blind god Hodr into killing Baldur with a dart of mistletoe, the one thing that could harm him.

keyScenes.title: Ragnarok
keyScenes.summary: The foretold final battle destroys the gods and the world, which is then reborn.

keyScenes.title: The Legend of the Volsungs
keyScenes.summary: Snorri retells Sigurd's slaying of Fafnir to explain a set of poetic kennings for gold.

readingOrder: Anthony Faulkes's Everyman translation (1987) is the standard complete English edition and a clear starting point for Snorri's retellings.

title: Mahabharata
author: Vyasa (traditional attribution)
description: The longest epic poem in existence, containing the Bhagavad Gita. Chronicles the Kurukshetra War and includes extensive Hindu mythology and philosophy.

characters.role: Pandava warrior who receives the Bhagavad Gita
characters.where: throughout; the Gita is in the Bhishma Parva (Book 6)

characters.role: Arjuna's charioteer and divine guide
characters.where: throughout, especially the Bhagavad Gita in Book 6

keyScenes.title: The Game of Dice
keyScenes.summary: Yudhishthira loses the Pandavas' kingdom, and Draupadi is humiliated, in a rigged dice game with the Kauravas.

keyScenes.title: The Bhagavad Gita
keyScenes.summary: On the eve of battle, Krishna counsels the grieving Arjuna on duty and the nature of the self.

keyScenes.title: The Death of Bhishma
keyScenes.summary: The Pandavas' grandsire falls to a combined assault by Arjuna and Shikhandi, but lingers to choose the moment of his death.

keyScenes.title: The Death of Karna
keyScenes.summary: Arjuna kills his secret half-brother Karna in the war's later stages.

keyScenes.title: The War's End
keyScenes.summary: The last Kaurava commanders fall, and a night raid slaughters the sleeping Pandava camp.

readingOrder: John D. Smith's abridged Penguin Classics translation (2009) is the most manageable entry point to the full epic; readers who want only the Gita can start with Eknath Easwaran's standalone translation.

title: Ramayana
author: Valmiki
description: The epic tale of Prince Rama, his exile, the abduction of his wife Sita by demon king Ravana, and his alliance with the monkey god Hanuman.

characters.role: protagonist, exiled prince of Ayodhya and avatar of Vishnu
devoted companion who leaps to Lanka to find Sita

keyScenes.title: Rama's Exile
keyScenes.summary: Rama is exiled to the forest for fourteen years to honor a promise his father made to his stepmother Kaikeyi.

keyScenes.title: The Abduction of Sita
keyScenes.summary: The demon king Ravana abducts Sita after luring Rama away with an illusory golden deer.

keyScenes.title: Hanuman's Leap to Lanka
keyScenes.summary: Hanuman crosses the ocean to find Sita and sets fire to Ravana's city.

keyScenes.title: The War with Ravana
keyScenes.summary: Rama, with an army of vanaras, kills Ravana and rescues Sita.

keyScenes.title: Sita's Trial and Rama's Reign
keyScenes.summary: Sita undergoes a trial by fire to prove her fidelity, and later tradition follows Rama's long reign and Sita's eventual banishment.

readingOrder: Arshia Sattar's abridged Penguin translation of Valmiki's Ramayana is a widely recommended, accessible starting point.

title: Rigveda
author: Various Vedic sages
description: The oldest of the four Vedas, containing 1,028 hymns to the Vedic deities including Indra, Agni, and Varuna. Foundation of Hindu religious tradition.

translators.name: Stephanie W. Jamison & Joel P. Brereton

characters.role: Thunder-wielding hero-king of the Devas who drinks soma, hurls the vajra, and releases the captive waters
Sacred fire, divine priest, and mediator carrying offerings from mortals to the gods
Prefigured in the fierce storm archer Rudra, lord of the wilderness, diseases, and healing balms
The wide-striding cosmic preserver whose three strides measure out earth, air, and the highest abode of light
Anticipated in the Golden Womb (Hiranyagarbha) and Prajapati, the singular Lord of all created things

keyScenes.title: Indra's Conquest of Vritra
keyScenes.summary: Intoxicated with triple soma, Indra grips his lightning bolt (vajra) and smashes the shoulders of Vritra the dragon-coiler, releasing the rivers that flow like bellowing cows to the sea.

keyScenes.title: The Hymn of Creation (Nasadiya Sukta)
keyScenes.summary: An awe-inspiring metaphysical inquiry: 'Then was neither non-existence nor existence... Who knows for certain? Who shall declare it? Whence was it born, and whence came this creation?'

keyScenes.title: The Sacrifice of the Cosmic Giant (Purusha Sukta)
keyScenes.summary: The thousand-headed giant Purusha is offered up by the gods; from his mind the moon was born, from his eye the sun, from his breath the wind, and from his feet the earth.

readingOrder: Start with Rigveda 1.32 (Indra slaying Vritra) for foundational mythic conflict, then read 10.129 (Nasadiya Sukta) for sublime cosmic philosophy, followed by 1.1 (the invocation of Agni).

title: Kojiki (Records of Ancient Matters)
author: O no Yasumaro
description: The oldest surviving chronicle of Japan, containing myths of creation, the divine couple Izanagi and Izanami, and the sun goddess Amaterasu.

characters.role: Great August Sun Goddess born from Izanagi's left eye, sovereign ruler of Takamagahara (High Plain of Heaven)
Fierce storm god born from Izanagi's nose, exiled for rebelliousness, who slays the eight-headed dragon Yamata-no-Orochi
The Male-Who-Invites, creator who churned the islands of Japan and journeyed to the underworld of Yomi
The Female-Who-Invites, creator who died giving birth to the fire god Kagutsuchi and became ruler of Yomi
Radiant moon god born from Izanagi's right eye during his purifying bath, assigned dominion over the night
Goddess of ecstatic dance who coaxes Amaterasu out of the Heavenly Rock Cave with laughter and performance
Benevolent earth ruler of Izumo who survives eighty jealous brothers and heals the White Hare of Inaba

keyScenes.title: Churning of the Primordial Island
keyScenes.summary: Standing upon the Floating Bridge of Heaven, Izanagi and Izanami stir the brine with the Jeweled Spear; drops falling from its tip congeal to form Onogoro Island.

keyScenes.title: The Descent into Yomi and the Great Cleansing
keyScenes.summary: Izanagi seeks Izanami in the land of the dead, breaks his promise not to gaze upon her rotting corpse, flees from thunder demons, and cleanses himself in the river, birthing Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo.

keyScenes.title: The Retreat into the Heavenly Rock Cave (Ama-no-Iwato)
keyScenes.summary: Grieved by Susanoo's violent rampages, Amaterasu conceals herself in the cave, plunging the world into darkness until Ame-no-Uzume's joyful dance brings laughter and coaxes her into the mirror's light.

keyScenes.title: Slaying the Yamata-no-Orochi
keyScenes.summary: Susanoo intoxicates the eight-headed serpent of Koshi with refined sake, hacks it to pieces with his sword, and discovers the legendary blade Ame-no-Murakumo (Kusanagi) in its tail.

readingOrder: Begin with Chapter 17 (the Heavenly Rock Cave) and Chapter 19 (the slaying of Yamata-no-Orochi), then read Chapters 3-10 for the island creation and Izanagi's eerie descent into Yomi.

title: Nihon Shoki (Chronicles of Japan)
author: Prince Toneri and O no Yasumaro
description: The second-oldest book of classical Japanese history, providing alternative versions of myths found in the Kojiki and additional material.

characters.role: Supreme solar ruler whose divine decree commands her grandson Ninigi to govern the terrestrial realm
characters.where: Age of the Gods, Books I-II

characters.role: Storm brother whose pact with Amaterasu produces divine offspring and whose trials shape ritual kingship
characters.where: Age of the Gods, Book I

characters.role: Primordial male deity whose ritual dialogues established ancient customs of marriage and purification
characters.where: Age of the Gods, Book I

characters.role: Primordial female deity whose binding covenant created mortal life cycles
characters.where: Age of the Gods, Book I

keyScenes.title: The Primordial Separation of Heaven and Earth
keyScenes.summary: The chronicle begins in stately classical prose: 'Of old, Heaven and Earth were not yet separated... forming a chaotic mass like an egg, wherein the clear and pure formed Heaven while the heavy and gross settled as Earth.'

keyScenes.title: The Descent of the Heavenly Grandson (Tenson Korin)
keyScenes.summary: Amaterasu entrusts Ninigi-no-Mikoto with the Three Sacred Treasures (Mirror, Jewel, Sword), saying: 'The Reed-Plain-1500-Autumn-Fair-Rice-Ear Land is the realm which my descendants shall govern.'

readingOrder: Read the opening cosmogony of Book I alongside Book II's account of the Tenson Korin (Divine Descent), the core mythological narrative of Japanese history.

title: Book of the Dead
author: Various Egyptian priests
description: A collection of funerary spells intended to assist the deceased in the afterlife. Major source for Egyptian underworld mythology and the weighing of the heart ceremony.

characters.role: Lord of the Underworld and supreme judge of souls in the afterlife
Jackal-headed master of embalming who guides the soul and balances the scale in the Hall of Truth
Ibis-headed divine scribe who records the verdict of the weighing of the heart
Protective prince and son of Osiris who introduces the vindicated soul to his enthroned father
Goddess of cosmic order whose white ostrich feather is the standard against which the heart is weighed
Supreme sun god aboard the solar barque whom the blessed dead accompany through eternity
Great enchantress whose magical wings protect the deceased from decay and danger

keyScenes.title: The Negative Confession (Declaration of Innocence)
keyScenes.summary: Standing before forty-two divine judges in the Hall of Ma'ati, the deceased recites specific denials of sins, demonstrating a life lived in harmony with Ma'at.

keyScenes.title: The Weighing of the Heart
keyScenes.summary: Anubis balances the deceased's heart (ib) against the feather of truth; Thoth stands poised with stylus and palette while Ammit waits to devour the sinful.

keyScenes.title: Entrance into the Field of Reeds (Aaru)
keyScenes.summary: Declared 'true of voice' (maa kheru), the spirit sails into the fertile celestial paradise to plow, reap, and feast beside Osiris forever.

readingOrder: Begin with Spell 125 (the Judgment and Weighing of the Heart), the moral core of Egyptian religion; then read Spell 1 for the tomb procession and Spell 110 for the vision of paradise in Aaru.

title: Pyramid Texts
author: Anonymous Egyptian priests
description: The oldest known religious texts in the world, carved on pyramid walls. Primary source for early Egyptian mythology and solar worship.

characters.role: Archetype of resurrected royalty whose triumph over death guarantees the pharaoh's immortality
Solar sovereign whose daily ascent the deceased pharaoh joins across the sky
Filial avenger whose restored Eye imparts divine vitality to the entombed monarch
Fierce god of desert storms whose conflict with Horus is ritually reconciled by the king
Sister-wife who gathers the dismembered Osiris and revives his royal ka
Protective goddess stationed at the head of the sarcophagus alongside Isis

keyScenes.title: The Proclamation of Immortality
keyScenes.summary: The priest declaims: 'O King, you have not departed dead, you have departed alive to sit upon the throne of Osiris!'

keyScenes.title: The Cannibal Hymn
keyScenes.summary: An archaic, thunderous ritual chant in the pyramid of Unas describing the pharaoh hunting, lassoing, and consuming the power of the gods to become supreme in heaven.

keyScenes.title: Ascension to the Imperishable Stars
keyScenes.summary: The king mounts the celestial ladder or soars as a divine falcon to join the circumpolar stars that never set or die.

readingOrder: Start with Utterance 213 for the fundamental funerary declaration of life after death, followed by Utterance 219 for the liturgical identification with Osiris, and Utterances 273-274 (the Cannibal Hymn) for ancient archaic royal ritual.

title: Popol Vuh
author: Anonymous K'iche' Maya
year: c. 1554-1558 CE (written; oral tradition much older)
description: The creation narrative of the K'iche' Maya, telling of the Hero Twins and multiple attempts by the gods to create humanity. The most important text of Mesoamerican mythology.

characters.role: Hunahpu and Xbalanque, miraculous twins who avenge their father and outwit the death-lords of Xibalba
Father of the twins, defeated in Xibalba, whose severed head in the calabash tree conceived the twins with Xquic
The Plumed Serpent (Gucumatz), sovereign creator god who speaks the cosmos into existence alongside Heart of Sky
Primordial sky deity representing celestial wisdom and priestly authority
Skeletal death-sovereign representing the lords of the underworld (One Death and Seven Death)
Monstrous death-bat of Xibalba who beheads Hunahpu during the trial of the Bat House

keyScenes.title: The Dawn of Creation and the Mud and Wood Races
keyScenes.summary: Heart of Sky and Plumed Serpent speak creation into existence; animals cannot praise them, mud people dissolve, and wooden mannequins lack hearts and minds and are destroyed in a flood of black pitch.

keyScenes.title: The Trials of the Underworld Houses
keyScenes.summary: The Hero Twins survive the Dark House, Razor House, Cold House, Jaguar House, and Fire House through clever tricks, animal alliances, and illusion.

keyScenes.title: The Decapitation in Bat House and the Ballgame
keyScenes.summary: Camazotz severs Hunahpu's head; Xbalanque carves a replacement gourd head, tricks the Xibalbans into using the real head as the ball, recovers it, and restores his brother.

keyScenes.title: Creation of the True Humans from Maize
keyScenes.summary: The creators find yellow and white ears of corn at Paxil; Grandmother Xmucane grinds the maize into dough, creating the flesh and strength of the first four true men.

readingOrder: Read Parts II and III first for the gripping epic of the Hero Twins descending into Xibalba, then read Part I for the primordial creation of the universe and Part IV for the sacred origin of humanity from corn.

title: Enuma Elish
author: Anonymous Babylonian priests
description: The Babylonian creation epic describing the rise of Marduk to supremacy among the gods and his creation of the world from the body of Tiamat.

characters.role: Champion of the gods who slays Tiamat and crafts the cosmos from her body
Primordial salt-water sea dragon and mother of monsters who wages war against the younger gods
God of wisdom and subterranean sweet waters (Ea) who slays Apsu and fathers Marduk
Primordial sky god sent first to confront Tiamat before fleeing her wrath
Lord of wind and storm whose supreme lordship passes to Marduk upon the victory

keyScenes.title: Tiamat's Uprising and the Army of Monsters
keyScenes.summary: Enraged by the death of her consort Apsu, Tiamat spawns an army of eleven horned serpents, dragons, and demons, bestowing the Tablet of Destinies upon Kingu.

keyScenes.title: Marduk Chosen as Divine Champion
keyScenes.summary: The elder gods assemble in terror; Marduk agrees to face Tiamat only on condition that the council grant him supreme and absolute rule over the universe.

keyScenes.title: The Cosmic Battle and Slaying of Tiamat
keyScenes.summary: Armed with the four winds and a divine net, Marduk traps Tiamat, drives the evil wind into her gaping maw, splits her heart with an arrow, and divides her corpse to fashion heaven and earth.

keyScenes.title: Creation of Humanity and Esagila
keyScenes.summary: From the blood of the slain rebel Kingu, Ea creates humankind to bear the labor of the gods, and the immortals build the great temple Esagila in Babylon to honor Marduk.

readingOrder: Start with Tablet IV for the climactic battle between Marduk and Tiamat, then read Tablet I for the primordial creation of sweet and salt waters, followed by Tablet VI for the creation of humankind.

title: Epic of Gilgamesh
author: Sin-leqi-unninni (standard version)
description: The oldest known epic literature, following the hero-king Gilgamesh and his companion Enkidu. Contains the earliest flood narrative and themes of mortality.

characters.role: protagonist, king of Uruk seeking immortality after Enkidu's death
Gilgamesh's companion, created by the gods to check his tyranny

keyScenes.title: Gilgamesh and Enkidu Meet
keyScenes.summary: Enkidu wrestles Gilgamesh to a standstill, and the two become inseparable friends.

keyScenes.title: The Slaying of Humbaba
keyScenes.summary: Gilgamesh and Enkidu journey to the Cedar Forest and kill its guardian, Humbaba.

keyScenes.title: The Bull of Heaven
keyScenes.summary: Gilgamesh spurns the goddess Ishtar, who sends the Bull of Heaven to punish him; the heroes kill it, and the gods condemn Enkidu to die.

keyScenes.title: The Death of Enkidu
keyScenes.summary: Enkidu falls ill and dies, plunging Gilgamesh into grief and fear of his own mortality.

keyScenes.title: The Quest for Immortality
keyScenes.summary: Gilgamesh seeks out the flood survivor Utnapishtim, fails to attain immortality, and returns to Uruk reconciled to his mortal fate.

readingOrder: Andrew George's Penguin Classics translation (1999) is the standard scholarly-accessible edition, with a clear introduction to the tablets' fragmentary state.

title: Aeneid
author: Virgil
description: The Roman national epic following Trojan hero Aeneas from the fall of Troy to the founding of Rome. Primary source for Roman mythology and religious practice.

characters.role: protagonist
Aeneas divine mother and guardian guide through his journey
implacable adversary of the Trojans stirring Carthage and Turnus
sovereign ruler of destiny who foretells Rome endless empire
calms the storm unleashed by Aeolus against the Trojan fleet
divine messenger who orders Aeneas to abandon Carthage and fulfill destiny

keyScenes.title: The Fall of Troy
keyScenes.summary: Aeneas recounts the Greeks' wooden horse and Troy's destruction, escaping with his father and son.

keyScenes.title: Dido and Aeneas
keyScenes.summary: Aeneas's affair with Queen Dido of Carthage ends when he abandons her to continue his divinely ordained journey.

keyScenes.title: The Descent to the Underworld
keyScenes.summary: Aeneas visits his dead father Anchises and glimpses the future glory of Rome.

keyScenes.title: The War in Latium
keyScenes.summary: Aeneas fights Turnus and the Latin peoples for the right to settle in Italy.

keyScenes.title: The Death of Turnus
keyScenes.summary: Aeneas kills Turnus in single combat, ending the epic.

readingOrder: Robert Fagles's 2006 translation is a vivid, widely read starting point; Sarah Ruden's 2021 translation is a tighter, line-for-line modern alternative.

title: Metamorphoses
author: Ovid
description: A narrative poem of transformations spanning from the creation of the world to the deification of Julius Caesar. Contains over 250 Greek and Roman myths.

characters.role: slays Medusa and rescues Andromeda
descends to the underworld for Eurydice
his death and the contest for his armor are narrated
loses the contest for Achilles' armor and takes his own life
his post-Troy journey and eventual deification are narrated
wins the contest for the arms of Achilles through forensic eloquence
burns on Mount Oeta after the poisoned robe of Nessus and ascends as a god
pursues Daphne whose transformation into a laurel originates his sacred tree
king of the gods who assumes mortal and animal forms across the transformation cycles

keyScenes.title: Apollo and Daphne
keyScenes.summary: Apollo's pursuit of the nymph Daphne ends with her transformation into a laurel tree.

keyScenes.title: Perseus and Andromeda
keyScenes.summary: Perseus rescues Andromeda from a sea monster and turns a rival suitor to stone with Medusa's head.

keyScenes.title: Orpheus and Eurydice
keyScenes.summary: Orpheus's underworld plea to reclaim Eurydice fails when he looks back too soon.

keyScenes.title: The Judgment of the Arms
keyScenes.summary: Ajax and Ulysses (Odysseus) contest for Achilles' armor in speeches before the Greek leaders; Ajax loses and kills himself.

keyScenes.title: The Deification of Aeneas
keyScenes.summary: Aeneas's mother Venus secures his transformation into the god Jupiter Indiges after his death in Italy.

readingOrder: A.D. Melville's Oxford World's Classics translation (1986) is a reliable, readable entry point; Charles Martin's 2004 verse translation is a livelier modern alternative.

title: Bibliotheca (Library)
author: Pseudo-Apollodorus
description: A comprehensive handbook of Greek mythology organized by genealogy. Invaluable reference for many myths not preserved elsewhere.

characters.role: Greatest of Greek heroes whose Twelve Labors, conquests, and apotheosis are systematically cataloged
Slayer of Medusa who rescues Andromeda from the sea-monster and fulfills the prophecy of Acrisius
Leader of the Argonauts who wins the Golden Fleece with the aid of the sorceress Medea
Athenian champion who clears the Isthmian road and slays the Minotaur in Knossos
King of Thebes who solves the Sphinx's riddle and unknowingly fulfills the tragic prophecy of Laius
Supreme Achaean warrior at Troy whose upbringing, invulnerability rites, and fatal duel with Hector are recorded

keyScenes.title: The Twelve Labors of Heracles
keyScenes.summary: The definitive classical handbook record of all twelve labors imposed by Eurystheus, from the Nemean Lion to Cerberus.

keyScenes.title: Perseus and the Gorgon Medusa
keyScenes.summary: Armed by Hermes and Athena with the reflective bronze shield and curved sickle, Perseus beheads the sleeping Medusa while looking only at her reflection.

keyScenes.title: Theseus in the Cretan Labyrinth
keyScenes.summary: Guided through the twisting dark by Ariadne's golden thread, Theseus kills the Minotaur with his bare hands and leads the Athenian youths to safety.

readingOrder: The Bibliotheca serves as the ancient world's primary mythological reference handbook. Read Book II for Heracles and Perseus, Book I.9 for Jason and the Argonauts, and Epitome I-V for Theseus and the Trojan War cycle.

title: Mythology: Timeless Tales of Gods and Heroes
author: Edith Hamilton
description: A widely influential introduction to Greek, Roman, and Norse mythology. Known for its accessible prose and emphasis on the human elements of ancient myths.

title: The Hero with a Thousand Faces
author: Joseph Campbell
description: The foundational work of comparative mythology introducing the concept of the 'monomyth' or hero's journey. Analyzes mythological narratives from cultures worldwide.

title: The Masks of God
author: Joseph Campbell
description: A four-volume comparative study of world mythology covering Primitive, Oriental, Occidental, and Creative aspects of human mythological expression.

title: The Golden Bough
author: James George Frazer
description: A pioneering work of comparative religion and mythology examining death-and-rebirth deities, sacred kingship, and ritual practices across cultures.

title: The Greek Myths
author: Robert Graves
description: A comprehensive retelling and analysis of Greek mythology with extensive commentary on sources and interpretations. Known for its matriarchal theory.

title: The Norse Myths
author: Kevin Crossley-Holland
description: An acclaimed retelling of the Norse myths from the Eddas, noted for its poetic prose and fidelity to the original spirit of the tales.

title: Gods and Pharaohs from Egyptian Mythology
author: Geraldine Harris
description: An accessible introduction to Egyptian mythology with beautiful illustrations, covering creation myths, the Osiris cycle, and pharaonic religion.

title: Hindu Myths: A Sourcebook
author: Wendy Doniger (O'Flaherty)
description: Translations of key texts from the Vedas, Brahmanas, Puranas, and epics, organized thematically around creation, destruction, and the lives of major deities.

title: Japanese Mythology
author: Juliet Piggott
description: An introduction to Shinto mythology from the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, covering the divine creation, the sun goddess Amaterasu, and legendary heroes.

title: Maya Cosmos: Three Thousand Years on the Shaman's Path
author: David Freidel, Linda Schele, & Joy Parker
description: A scholarly exploration of Maya mythology combining archaeological evidence, art history, and deciphered hieroglyphic texts.

title: Ancient Iraq
author: Georges Roux
description: A comprehensive history of Mesopotamia from prehistory to the Hellenistic period, including detailed coverage of Sumerian, Babylonian, and Assyrian mythology.

title: The Oxford Dictionary of World Mythology
author: Arthur Cotterell
description: A comprehensive reference work covering mythological figures, themes, and narratives from cultures across the globe.

title: The Complete World of Greek Mythology
author: Richard Buxton
description: A beautifully illustrated scholarly overview of Greek mythology, examining myths in their cultural, religious, and artistic contexts.

title: Táin Bó Cúailnge
author: Anonymous (Ulster Cycle)
year: c. 8th century CE (oral tradition; earliest manuscripts 12th century CE)
description: The central epic of the Ulster Cycle of Irish mythology, telling how Queen Medb of Connacht invaded Ulster to seize the Brown Bull of Cooley, and how the young hero Cu Chulainn held the province alone against her army.

characters.role: Ulster's champion, defends the province alone
prophesies to Cu Chulainn and later hinders him in battle

keyScenes.title: The Pillow Talk
keyScenes.summary: Queen Medb goes to war with Ulster after a boasting contest with her husband over their wealth turns on the Brown Bull of Cooley's equal.

keyScenes.title: Cu Chulainn's Single Combats
keyScenes.summary: With Ulster's warriors disabled by a curse, the young Cu Chulainn holds off Medb's army alone in a series of ford duels.

keyScenes.title: The Death of Ferdiad
keyScenes.summary: Cu Chulainn is forced to kill his foster-brother and friend Ferdiad in a grueling multi-day duel.

keyScenes.title: The Battle of the Bulls
keyScenes.summary: The Brown Bull of Cooley and Connacht's White-Horned Bull fight to the death as Ulster's men finally rise to rout Medb's army.

readingOrder: Thomas Kinsella's 1969 translation is the classic English starting point; Ciaran Carson's 2007 Penguin Classics translation is a livelier modern alternative.

title: Hittite Myths
author: Harry A. Hoffner Jr. (translator; ed. Gary M. Beckman)
description: The standard English translation of Hittite mythological texts, covering both the Anatolian myths preserved in rituals (the Illuyanka tales, the disappearance of Telipinu and other vanishing deities) and the Hurrian Kumarbi cycle translated into Hittite. Hoffner marks gaps and damaged passages throughout.

characters.role: the Storm-god, defeated and then victorious against the serpent; the Hurrian Teššub of the Kumarbi cycle
the god whose angry departure starves the land
the mother goddess who sends the bee to find Telipinu
prepares the feast that traps the serpent
performs the rite that soothes Telipinu's anger

keyScenes.title: The Serpent at the Feast
keyScenes.summary: Inara lays out a feast; the serpent and its children eat and drink until they cannot squeeze back into their hole, and the mortal Hupašiya binds them for the Storm-god.

keyScenes.title: The Bee Finds Telipinu
keyScenes.summary: After the Sun-god's eagle and the Storm-god himself fail, Hannahanna's bee finds Telipinu asleep in a meadow near Lihzina and stings him awake.

readingOrder: Start with the Illuyanka tales and the Disappearance of Telipinu, which are short and Anatolian; then read the Song of Kumarbi and the Song of Ullikummi together as a Hurrian cycle.

title: The Kumarbi Cycle (Song of Kumarbi, Song of Hedammu, Song of Ullikummi)
author: Anonymous Hurrian poets; Hittite translations from the Hattusa archives
year: Hurrian originals probably before the 14th c. BCE; surviving Hittite copies 14th-13th c. BCE
language: Hittite (translated from Hurrian), with Hurrian-language fragments
description: A cycle of Hurrian songs about the struggle for kingship in heaven between Kumarbi, father of the gods, and the storm-god Teššub. Known mainly from Hittite translations found at Hattusa (CTH 344-348), it is the closest Near Eastern parallel to the succession myth of Hesiod's Theogony. Every song in the cycle is fragmentary.

characters.role: father of the gods, who seizes kingship from Anu and plots against Teššub
characters.where: Song of Kumarbi (CTH 344); Song of Ullikummi (CTH 345)

characters.role: the first king in heaven, overthrown by Anu
Teššub, the storm-god born from Kumarbi, who wins kingship
Teššub's sister, who tries to seduce Hedammu and Ullikummi
characters.where: Song of Hedammu (CTH 348); Song of Ullikummi (CTH 345)

keyScenes.title: The Succession in Heaven
keyScenes.summary: Alalu reigns nine years before Anu overthrows him; Anu reigns nine years before Kumarbi bites off his loins and swallows the seed of the storm-god.

keyScenes.title: The Stone Monster on Upelluri's Shoulder
keyScenes.summary: Kumarbi fathers a basalt giant on a great rock and hides it on the shoulder of the world-bearing giant Upelluri, where it grows until it reaches the sky.

keyScenes.title: The Ancient Copper Cutter
keyScenes.summary: Ea brings out the tool that once separated heaven from earth and cuts Ullikummi's feet from Upelluri's shoulder.

readingOrder: Read the Song of Kumarbi first, then the Song of Ullikummi; the Song of Hedammu is more fragmentary and best read after both.
